description:
🚀 Welcome to our team for the "Abandoned but Not Forgotten" challenge! We are a Universal Event team aiming to create an innovative, interactive tool to discover, map, and breathe new life into forgotten or decommissioned space artifacts and historical NASA data. 

Whether you love frontend development, backend engineering, data science, or creative UI/UX design and storytelling, we need you! Let's combine our skills to preserve space history. Join us and let's build something epic!
summary: Secret Diaries of NASA’s Space Machines is an interactive 7-slide digital storybook designed for school-age students (ages 8–14) to discover the real science behind NASA’s retired spacecraft on the Moon and Mars. Many young learners assume equipment left in space is simply "space junk," missing the extraordinary engineering breakthroughs each artifact represents. Using official NASA mission archives, our project brings four iconic machines to life—the Apollo 11 Lunar Module Eagle, the electric Lunar Roving Vehicle (Moon Buggy), the Spirit and Opportunity Mars rovers, and the Ingenuity Mars Helicopter—through first-person diary entries, real unaltered NASA imagery, clear scientific takeaways, and an interactive quiz.
details:
1. What It Does & How It Works: Secret Diaries of NASA’s Space Machines is an interactive 7-slide digital storybook built for school-age students (ages 8–14). Instead of treating retired space hardware as "space junk," it brings four real NASA spacecraft on the Moon and Mars to life through first-person diary entries, real NASA mission photography, clear engineering takeaways, and an interactive quiz at the end.

    Benefits & Intended Impact: Young learners often struggle with technical mission logs. By giving iconic machines—the Apollo 11 Eagle Lander, Apollo Lunar Roving Vehicle (Moon Buggy), Spirit and Opportunity Mars Rovers, and Ingenuity Mars Helicopter—a relatable voice, students easily remember the physics and engineering breakthroughs that made planetary exploration possible.

    Tools Used & Design Considerations: We researched official NASA mission archives (nssdc.gsfc.nasa.gov and science.nasa.gov), verified authentic unaltered NASA mission photos, and designed a high-contrast space-themed slide deck in Microsoft PowerPoint (exported to PDF for instant browser access across classrooms and mobile devices).
